### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. hypoparathyroidism-retardation-dysmorphism syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.732)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-389977)

**Proposed mechanism:** TBCE (HGNC:11582) —DISRUPTS→ Endoplasmic Reticulum-Associated Degradation (ERAD) pathway (GO:0030438); Endoplasmic Reticulum-Associated Degradation (ERAD) pathway (GO:0030438) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004308); Endoplasmic Reticulum-Associated Degradation (ERAD) pathway (GO:0030438) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Endoplasmic Reticulum-Associated Degradation (ERAD) pathway (GO:0030438) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoparathyroidism (HP:0000772); Endoplasmic Reticulum-Associated Degradation (ERAD) pathway (GO:0030438) —LEADS_TO→ Dysmorphism (HP:0001999). Loss-of-function mutations in TBCE disrupt the ERAD pathway, leading to the accumulation of misfolded proteins and cellular stress, ultimately manifesting as the overlapping phenotypes of short stature, intellectual disability, hypoparathyroidism, and dysmorphism.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of functionally distinct pathogenic variants in TBCE that result in loss-of-function for Kenny-Caffey syndrome but gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects for hypoparathyroidism-retardation-dysmorphism syndrome, or vice-versa, would falsify this hypothesis of a shared loss-of-function mechanism. _(variant: Presence of common variants in the TBCE gene with frequencies >1% in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of TBCE in the ERAD pathway provides a potential therapeutic target for both conditions. Modulating ERAD pathway function could ameliorate the cellular dysfunction and downstream phenotypes associated with mutations in this gene.

#### 2. encephalopathy, progressive, with amyotrophy and optic atrophy  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.729)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-389977)

**Proposed mechanism:** TBCE (HGNC:11582) —DISRUPTS→ Nuclear envelope structure and function (REACT:R-HSA-72760); Nuclear envelope structure and function (REACT:R-HSA-72760) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004322); Nuclear envelope structure and function (REACT:R-HSA-72760) —LEADS_TO→ Optic atrophy (HP:0000647); Nuclear envelope structure and function (REACT:R-HSA-72760) —LEADS_TO→ Progressive muscle atrophy (HP:0003219); Nuclear envelope structure and function (REACT:R-HSA-72760) —LEADS_TO→ Encephalopathy (HP:0001295). Loss-of-function mutations in TBCE disrupt nuclear envelope structure and function, leading to overlapping phenotypes of short stature (Kenny-Caffey syndrome) and optic atrophy, progressive muscle atrophy, and encephalopathy (progressive encephalopathy with amyotrophy and optic atrophy).

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in TBCE in individuals with either disease that are not loss-of-function (e.g., dominant-negative or gain-of-function) would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Any pathogenic variant in TBCE with a gnomAD allele frequency > 0.001)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of TBCE in nuclear envelope integrity could reveal common therapeutic targets for both Kenny-Caffey syndrome and progressive encephalopathy with amyotrophy and optic atrophy, potentially focusing on pathways that stabilize the nuclear envelope or compensate for its dysfunction.

**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-389977)

**Proposed mechanism:** TBCE (HGNC:11701) —DISRUPTS→ Golgi apparatus function (GO:0005794); TBCD (HGNC:11700) —DISRUPTS→ Golgi apparatus function (GO:0005794); Golgi apparatus function (GO:0005794) —LEADS_TO→ Protein trafficking (GO:0006886); Protein trafficking (GO:0006886) —LEADS_TO→ Microcephaly (HP:0000252); Protein trafficking (GO:0006886) —LEADS_TO→ Brain atrophy (HP:0002059); Protein trafficking (GO:0006886) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324); Protein trafficking (GO:0006886) —LEADS_TO→ Optic atrophy (HP:0000647); Protein trafficking (GO:0006886) —LEADS_TO→ Cortical thinning (HP:0012443). Loss-of-function mutations in both TBCE (Kenny-Caffey syndrome) and TBCD (early-onset progressive diffuse brain atrophy-microcephaly-muscle weakness-optic atrophy syndrome) disrupt Golgi apparatus function, which in turn impairs protein trafficking, leading to a shared set of neurodevelopmental and muscular phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of pathogenic variants in TBCE and TBCD in individuals diagnosed with these respective syndromes, or demonstration that these genes function independently in entirely separate cellular pathways without any shared downstream effects on protein trafficking or Golgi apparatus integrity. _(variant: Any common variant (AF > 0.01) in the coding regions of TBCE or TBCD identified in gnomAD.)_
